risk_if_not_implemented: Without Heterogeneity, security may be bolted on rather than designed in, resulting in structural weaknesses that are costly to remediate and easy to exploit. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Concentration / Single-Point Dependency Failure (R-OR-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Product Defect / Design Failure (MT-23).

compensating_control_1.name: Defense-In-Depth (DiD) Architecture
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to implement security functions as a layered structure minimizing interactions between layers of the design and avoiding any dependence by lower layers on the functionality or correctness of higher layers.
compensating_control_1.justification: Defense-In-Depth (DiD) Architecture (SEA-06) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Heterogeneity (SEA-22) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Technology applicability. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to implement network segmentation within network architectures to isolate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) from other network resources.
compensating_control_2.justification: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation) (NET-06) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of Heterogeneity (SEA-22) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
